sections.title: Lesson 12.1: Associating With and Leaving a Member Firm
sections.overview: Becoming an associated person of a FINRA member firm requires the firm to file Form U4 with FINRA/CRD, with registration effective only upon passing the required qualification exams. Separation from a firm is documented via Form U5. Disclosure on both forms is critical—willful misstatements can result in a lifetime bar—and certain prior events (statutory disqualification) can prevent registration entirely.
key_concepts: Form U4 — filed by the member firm to register an associated person with FINRA; registration is not effective until qualification exam(s) are passed.

U4 contents: name/address/aliases, 5-year residency history, 10-year employment history (full-time education counts within the 10-year work history), disclosure of charges/convictions, and Disclosure Reporting Pages (DRPs) for any 'yes' answers.
NOT required on U4: marital status, educational background (beyond what falls inside the 10-year employment history), U.S. citizenship.
Two firm requirements: (1) sponsorship by a member BD, and (2) complete and truthful disclosure.
Exam retake schedule: 30-day waiting period after a failed attempt; after 3 consecutive failures, a 180-day wait before the 4th attempt.
Exam window: filing the U4 with an exam request opens a 120-day window to complete the exam; if it lapses, the window must be reopened (no new U4 required).
SIE validity: SIE remains valid for 4 years to take a top-off or re-affiliate; after 4 years the SIE must be retaken.
U4 amendments: most events filed within 30 days; statutory disqualification events within 10 business days.
Background check: member firm must investigate the applicant's reputation, character, education, qualifications, and experience before filing.

Fingerprinting: required for persons in sales, those handling cash/customer securities, and all directors/officers/partners; submitted to U.S. Attorney General. Clerical/ministerial persons with no access to cash, securities, or books of original entry are exempt. Persons selling only mutual funds, variable annuities, or DPPs are exempt.
Form U5: filed within 30 days of termination with CRD; copy to former employee within the same 30 days. Late filing triggers fees.
U5 termination reasons: Discharged, Permitted to Resign, Deceased, Voluntary, Other. Discharged / Permitted to Resign / Other require a detailed explanation.
Partial termination (U5): used when an associated person drops some but not all registrations (e.g., a principal stepping down to RR-only).
U5 amendment for statutory disqualification: within 10 business days of discovery.
Post-termination jurisdiction: FINRA retains jurisdiction for 2 years to investigate and require testimony.
Two-year requalification rule: a terminated person may re-affiliate within 2 years without retaking exams.

Maintaining Qualifications Program (MQP) — under amended FINRA Rule 1240, a terminated registered person may extend the requalification window up to 5 years by completing annual CE through FINRA's FinPro system.

Military service: representatives on regular active military duty are placed in a special inactive status until 90 days after discharge; the 2-year re-affiliation clock starts at the end of that period.
Post-termination commissions: trailing commissions allowed under a pre-existing contract (typical for retirees, payable to heirs) but only on existing business — no new business.

Statutory Disqualification (SD) triggers: expulsion/suspension by an SRO (domestic or foreign equivalent); SEC or foreign regulator order suspending/revoking registration or barring association; being found the cause of another's expulsion/suspension; willful misstatements on registration applications; felony conviction (any) or securities/money-related misdemeanor within the past 10 years; court injunctions barring acting as IA, underwriter, BD, etc.
Bankruptcy or an unsatisfied lien alone is NOT disqualifying — but failure to disclose it IS.
BrokerCheck: CRD-based public disclosure of registered persons' disciplinary history; FINRA member websites must link to BrokerCheck.
rules: FINRA Rule 1010 series — Member Application and Associated Person Registration (U4 filing).
FINRA Rule 1122 — Filing of Misleading Information as to Membership or Registration (willful misstatements may bar for life).
FINRA Rule 3110(e) — Member firm responsibility to investigate applicants for registration (background check).
FINRA Rule 8312 — BrokerCheck disclosure requirements.
FINRA Rule 2263 — Arbitration disclosure to associated persons signing U4.
FINRA Rule 4530 — Reportable events to FINRA.
Securities Exchange Act §3(a)(39) — Statutory disqualification definition.
SEC Rule 17f-2 — Fingerprinting of securities industry personnel.
Article III, FINRA By-Laws — Qualifications of Members and Associated Persons.
Article V, FINRA By-Laws — Registered Representatives and Associated Persons (U4/U5 mechanics, 2-year jurisdiction).
formulas: Exam retake wait = 30 days after each of the first 3 failures; 180 days after the 3rd consecutive failure.
Exam window after U4 filed = 120 days to pass.
SIE shelf life = 4 years (to pass top-off OR to re-affiliate before retaking SIE).
U4 amendment deadline = 30 days (standard) / 10 business days (statutory disqualification).
U5 filing deadline = 30 days from termination date.
Post-termination FINRA jurisdiction = 2 years (extendable up to 5 via MQP).
Military inactive status ends = 90 days after discharge; 2-year clock starts thereafter.
mnemonics: '4-4-4 SIE life': SIE valid 4 years to top-off, 4 years to re-affiliate, files 4 years' worth of memory in your head.
'30/10' for amendments: 30 days standard, 10 business days for Statutory Disqualification (the more serious, the faster).
U5 termination reasons — 'D-P-D-V-O': Discharged, Permitted to resign, Deceased, Voluntary, Other (only Deceased and Voluntary need NO explanation).
'Sales or Safe' = fingerprint required: anyone in Sales or with access to the Safe (cash/securities). Pure clerical = no print.
'Felony any / Misdemeanor money' — within 10 years = statutory DQ.

sections.title: Lesson 12.2: Ongoing Expectations of Representatives of Registered Persons
sections.overview: Once registered, an associated person operates under continuous obligations: supervision by registered principals, prompt handling of customer complaints, mandatory continuing education, and pre-approval/disclosure of outside business activities and private securities transactions. Strict caps apply to gifts, gratuities, and political contributions to prevent conflicts of interest and pay-to-play arrangements.
key_concepts: Principals: Anyone managing or supervising any aspect of a member's investment banking or securities business (including training) must register as a principal. Non-sole-proprietorship firms must employ at least two registered principals.
Principal duties: approving new accounts, approving margin/options accounts, reviewing/approving communications, reviewing trading activity, hiring/training, responding to all written complaints.

Customer complaint definition: a written statement by a customer (or someone acting on the customer's behalf) alleging a grievance arising out of/connected with a securities transaction; includes electronic communications.
Complaint handling: route to principal, branch manager, or compliance; if resolved to both parties' satisfaction, no further action needed.
Quarterly complaint report: members file a list of all written complaints with FINRA within 15 days of each calendar quarter-end.
Complaint record retention: copies kept for 4 years after resolution.

Continuing Education — Firm Element: annual in-house training plan tailored to firm's business, regulatory developments, and personnel needs; required for all registered persons with public contact; must be completed by December 31 (firm may set earlier deadline); failure can result in license deactivation.

Continuing Education — Regulatory Element (post-2022 amendment to FINRA Rule 1240): now an ANNUAL requirement administered by FINRA; content varies by registration category (RR vs. principal). Failure to complete causes deactivation of registration until requirements are met. (Old rule of 'every 3 years after the 2nd anniversary' is superseded.)

Outside Business Activities (OBAs) — FINRA Rule 3270: an associated person may not be an employee, independent contractor, sole proprietor, officer, director, or partner of another person or business, or receive compensation from any other person as a result of any business activity outside the scope of the relationship with their firm, unless prior WRITTEN NOTICE is provided to the member.
OBA exception: passive investments and activities through a non-controlled entity are not OBAs; uncompensated volunteer work generally does not require notice.

Private Securities Transactions ('selling away') — FINRA Rule 3280: any sale of securities outside an associated person's regular business and employing member. Prior written notice required, including description of transaction, role, and whether compensation will be received.
PST with compensation: firm must approve in writing; if approved, firm must record the transaction on its books and supervise it as if it were its own; if disapproved, the person may not participate.
PST without compensation: firm must acknowledge receipt of written notice; firm may impose conditions or prohibit participation.
PST exclusion: transactions on behalf of immediate family with no compensation received are not PSTs.
Gifts & Gratuities — FINRA Rule 3220: cap of $100 per person per year for business-related cash or non-cash gifts; not contingent on sales; employing firm's prior approval required.

Gift cap EXCEPTIONS (over $100 permitted): occasional non-cash items (meals, seminars, entertainment tickets) where a rep of the giver attends = business entertainment; reminder advertising (logo items of nominal value); life-event gifts (weddings, births, retirement). All must be reasonable.

Political Contributions — MSRB Rule G-37 (Pay-to-Play): municipal firms prohibited from engaging in municipal securities business with an issuer for 2 YEARS after a contribution to an official of that issuer by the firm, an MFP, or a firm-controlled PAC.
G-37 scope: applies to NEGOTIATED underwritings and financial advisory work — NOT to competitive bid underwritings.

Municipal Finance Professional (MFP): associated person engaged in municipal underwriting, trading, sales, financial advisory, research, advice, or public-investor communications. Sales-only-to-individuals or clerical persons are NOT MFPs.
G-37 de minimis: MFPs may contribute up to $250 per election to candidates for whom they are ELIGIBLE TO VOTE. The de minimis does NOT apply to the firm itself (a firm cannot vote).
FINRA Rule 3210: registered-person brokerage accounts at other firms require written notice to employer and consent; duplicate confirms/statements furnished on request.

FINRA Rule 3240: borrowing/lending between RR and customer prohibited unless (a) within enumerated permitted relationships (immediate family, bank/lender in the business of lending, business relationship outside the BD relationship, etc.) AND (b) written firm approval.
rules: FINRA Rule 1240 — Continuing Education (Regulatory Element now ANNUAL per amendment effective 3/15/2022; Maintaining Qualifications Program extends re-affiliation window to 5 years).
FINRA Rule 3110 — Supervision (principal responsibilities).
FINRA Rule 3110.18 — Remote Inspections Pilot Program (effective 7/1/2024 – 6/30/2027): eligible firms may satisfy branch inspection obligations remotely with WSPs and FINRA reporting.

FINRA Rule 3110.19 — Residential Supervisory Location (effective 6/1/2024): a registered person's residence may qualify as a non-branch location with periodic (not annual) inspections if conditions met (no customer funds, no public signage, eligible-person status).
FINRA Rule 3210 — Accounts at other broker-dealers.
FINRA Rule 3220 — Influencing or Rewarding Employees of Others ($100 gift limit).
FINRA Rule 3240 — Borrowing from / lending to customers.
FINRA Rule 3270 — Outside Business Activities of Registered Persons (prior written notice).
FINRA Rule 3280 — Private Securities Transactions (selling away).
FINRA Rule 4111 — Restricted Firm Obligations (effective 1/1/2022; annual designation of restricted firms requiring deposit).
FINRA Rule 4513 — Records of Written Customer Complaints (4-year retention).
FINRA Rule 4530 — Reporting Requirements (quarterly complaint report within 15 days of quarter-end).
MSRB Rule G-37 — Political Contributions and Prohibitions on Municipal Securities Business (2-year ban; $250 de minimis for MFPs in eligible-to-vote elections).
MSRB Rule G-20 — Gifts, Gratuities and Non-Cash Compensation.
formulas: Gift cap = $100 per person, per year (business-related, non-sales-contingent, with firm pre-approval).
MFP political contribution de minimis = $250 per election, per candidate the MFP can vote for (firm itself: $0).
G-37 ban = 2 years of no municipal securities business with the issuer after a triggering contribution.
Firm Element CE = at least annually, completed by December 31.
Quarterly complaint filing = within 15 days of calendar quarter-end.
Customer complaint record retention = 4 years after resolution.
Branch inspection cycle = OSJ annually; non-OSJ branch every 3 years; non-branch periodic (Remote Inspection Pilot and RSL designation may modify).
mnemonics: 'Selling Away = Tell Today': any private securities transaction requires PRIOR written notice to the firm.
'$100 / $250 / 2': $100 gift cap, $250 MFP political de minimis, 2-year G-37 ban.
OBA vs. PST — OBA = outside JOB (3270); PST = outside SECURITIES sale (3280).
'A-R-R-R-H-R' principal duties: Approve accounts, Review trading, Review communications, Respond to complaints, Hire/train, Review options/margin.
G-37 'Negotiated, Not Bid' — pay-to-play rule bites only on negotiated underwritings and financial advisory work.
Regulatory Element = 'Annual Anniversary' (post-2022, replaces old 2-yr/3-yr cycle).
